dataset.roi_source: retained production frame-index bounds for dynamic thumbnails; fixed bounds seeded from the first successful static frame

VERIFIED: The offline ROI matrix processed the same 106 retained images across two fresh parameter variants and two preprocessing branches without camera, TCP, firmware, or hardware access.
On the six retained dynamic failure thumbnails, adaptive_wide plus blue_2x detected 4/6, while the gray_1x control detected 0/6; default blue_2x detected 1/6.
The adaptive_wide plus blue_2x candidate had a dynamic processing p95 of 12.686 ms and a static processing p95 of 15.063 ms, both below the 33.333333 ms offline budget.
The candidate retained 100/100 detections on the static ROI sample; this is a static regression result, not a dynamic continuity result.
INFERENCE: Restricting the candidate to the retained ROI appears to remove most of the full-frame adaptive processing cost, making this composite candidate feasible for one matched real rerun.
The recovery cannot be attributed to adaptive threshold widening alone: the candidate also uses the blue channel, and the six-thumbnail sample cannot establish the interaction or causal mechanism.
INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: Six failure thumbnails are not a continuous run and cannot establish detection ratio, maximum pose gap, or real-time behavior on a fresh run.
The ROI was supplied from prior production diagnostics, so this benchmark tests detector recovery inside a known ROI; it does not prove that the production tracker will maintain that ROI.
No candidate has been deployed to the production PoseTracker, and no real-car improvement or B3 pass is established.

decision.next_action: After explicit hardware authorization, run one matched 1080p capture comparing the unchanged production path against this bounded ROI candidate; retain full frame index, failure frames, and independent observation gates.
